FILE CLAUDE.md
# RimWorld 1.6 — Jawa scavenger clan on a desert world

**Read `infrastructure/agents/CHARTER.md`** — the whole process rulebook — and your
own window file: `infrastructure/agents/CONDUCTOR.md` (the Conductor, with the owner); the
autonomous builder is the Relentless Pipeline (`src/RimMandrake/rimflow/relentless.py`), whose places hold
Relentless-style Builder/Judge workers from MandrakeWorkflows (`relentless/workers/`; owner 2026-11-03). Game cycle:
`infrastructure/GAME_STATE_WORKFLOW.md`. **Models: the ladder lives in
`infrastructure/agents/Agent_Policy.md` and nowhere else; never restate it.**

This file holds RULES and POINTERS only. Each rule's full text, the incidents behind it
and its measurements live in the file it points at:

| topic | full text |
|---|---|
| biome, roster, sea, naming-tier rulings | `design/RimMandrake/biome_rulings.md` |
| north star, LLM transport, pits, DLC, git, code review, art, bridge, savegame options | `design/RimMandrake/standing_rulings.md` |
| instruments that return a confident wrong number | `infrastructure/state/facts/instrument_traps.md` |
| tools with surprising side effects | `infrastructure/state/facts/tool_traps.md` |
| creature flight (stat, race flags, flip-book) | `skills/rimworld-modding/references/flight.md` |
| ticking, `MayRequire`, csproj, patch behaviour | `skills/rimworld-modding/references/project-engine-facts.md` |

## How we debug — owner, 2026-10-01

*"I really do mean stop and start working a new way."* Every mod gets a functional script
and is debugged through it; every live poking session ends by writing what it learned —
including informative false theories — into that script. Agents write and approve those
scripts. North-star bars: agents may add regression checks and new bars (owner 2026-10-26,
*"Both autonomy questions are yes"*; `delegation_policy.md` §2.1); loosening a bar stays his. The 2026-10-01 build pause was
**lifted by the owner 2026-10-02** (*"Build pause is lifted."*); every new mod still ships with
its first script. Process: `design/RimMandrake/debug_process.md`.

## 🔴 There is no worldgen feature, in any version — owner, 2026-08-15

- **OUT, permanently:** any automated or programmatic worldgen; worldgen as a
  player-facing capability. ⛔ v2 is not a parking space for it — mark such work
  dead, never deferred.
- 🔑 **Players never generate anything. They receive a savegame holding the fixed
  world** — one hand-made world, frozen, shipped. A faction, ideoligion or setting
  absent when it freezes is absent from every player's game forever.
- ⛔ **Do not build anything that produces ALTERNATIVE planets** (owner, 2026-08-18).
  No seed sweeps, no variants, no knobs that could roll a second world. ✅ Author
  THE map, judged by realism first, iterated by LOOKING (`worldview.py`); target and
  references: `design/Jawa/worldbuilding/the_one_map.md`.

## 🔴 A BIOME WITH ZERO TILES IS NOT A DEFECT — owner, 2026-09-20, said repeatedly

> *"Correct we will repaint the whole world when all the biomes are in. **You don't need
> to keep rediscovering this.**"* · *"Don't worry about worldmap painting. Once we have
> all the biomes in mods we will do the painting once and for all."*

- **The planet is painted ONCE, at the end**, after every biome's content is mod-migrated.
  A BiomeDef of ours on 0 tiles is the EXPECTED state: not a finding, not a defect.
- ⛔ Never repoint owned content at a donor def to make it appear on today's map; ⛔ never
  cite a tile count as evidence that something is or is not built. Keep the paint list
  (`BIOME_PAINT_ONCE_AT_THE_END_1`). **About to report one of our biomes on zero tiles? You
  have rediscovered this. Stop.** (It cost three reconciliation passes.)
- 🔴 **`world/ASHKARR_WORLDMAP_tiles.csv` is a RECORD, not the planet** — *"It is a RECORD of
  the planet, not a rival to it."* It tells you the planet on its export date; the live
  system is the only instrument for "right now".

Full text and incidents: `design/RimMandrake/biome_rulings.md`.

## 🔴 Relentless builds and accepts the work that needs building, FlowWorks and GSS included; FOUNDRY is retired — owner, by card 2026-11-02

*"What should happen to FOUNDRY?"* → **Retire it.** One builder: Relentless builds, proves (its game_prove lane, `relentless_live_round.py`, is the acceptance sweep for every mod) and closes; the Conductor talks with him and keeps only items that need him live (needs=owner, an L4 look, flyer live tests). Design still to be argued out goes to the Designer (`src/RimMandrake/rimflow/roles/designer.md`); ops alarms to Operations. The daily findings judging and the Friday memory sweep are `rm-findings-judge.timer`. FOUNDRY is not a seat: `rimflow` maps it to the Conductor/Relentless shared key (`RETIRED_SEATS` in `cli.py`), as does the FlowWorks lane (`infrastructure/state/flowworks_lane.json`, field `seat`). Supersedes the 2026-10-28 FOUNDRY-owns-FlowWorks ruling. Narrowed by the owner, 2026-11-06: *"It's a builder/test-builder/judge pipeline, not an everything pipeline...."* Relentless is for work that needs building, a built test and a judge; approved art, deploys, one-off commands and readings are done directly by the Conductor or a helper.

## Biomes, rosters and seas — owner rulings (full text: `design/RimMandrake/biome_rulings.md`)

- 🔑 **Search `src/` and the roster before FILING or designing** (user-level rule; here it is `src/` and the roster).
- **Say which greatbole you mean:** `RM_Greatbole` (fellable tree) · `RUT_GreatboleHeartwood`
  (the mineable blob) · `RUT_GreatboleCore` (1×1 bookkeeping marker).
- 🔑 **An animal belongs to ONE biome unless there is an IN-GAME reason** — *"Animals sound be
  biome-specific unless there is an in-game reason"*; *"I meant pick one arid home."* A hole
  in a roster is filled with a NEW creature. 🔴🔴 **But EVICTIONS ARE STOPPED** — *"Let's stop
  evictions right now"*; *"This is a human review process issue."* No pass edits a roster to
  enforce this; multi-homed species are rows on that biome's own sheet at its sitting.
  🔑 **If consecutive questions to him each add a clause to a procedure, STOP** — it is review work.
- 🔑 **A sea biome describes BOTH its floor and its catch** (*"what you encounter as an animal
  there … as well as what you can FISH out"*); only fish-sized creatures owe a catch, and
  *"All the fishables should also be alive and moving around in the depths (this is true for
  ALL seas)."*
- 🔴 **The ship is the only way down and back** — *"It's ship or nothing."* The ship flies to
  its own planet layer, `RM_SeabedLayer`; `RM_SeaDiveHatch` is a leftover
  (`SEA_DIVE_HATCH_REMOVE_1`).
- **Every BiomeDef with a roster sets `animalDensity`** (unset = 0 = no animals ever spawn).
  Parse `<wildAnimals>`/`<wildPlants>` as XML ELEMENTS, never by counting `<li>`.
- 🔑 **A review sheet's `cut` is scoped to THAT SHEET'S BIOME, never the planet.**
- 🔴 **An `RM_` twin's real cast is PATCH-ADDED** (`UtinniPatches/Patches/WildAnimals_<Biome>.xml`);
  reading BiomeDefs alone sees the wrong half.

## 🔑 "Star Wars style" naming is NOT Star Wars IP — owner, 2026-09-22 (Q11a)

*"The fact that we will use "star wars style" naming doesn't mean they have to live in the star
wars layer."* An **invented** exotic name lives in the franchise-free `RM_` tier; only a
**genuine canon** name is IP and routes through the Utinni patch layer. A `RM_` roster is rich
enough to stand alone — never a thin fallback. 🔑 When a tier or provenance question starts
generating sub-questions, **ask whether the CATEGORY is needed at all** before adjudicating
inside it. A donor mod's defName is not a canon source; verify canon with the Wookieepedia
search API. Authority: `biome_mod_architecture.md` §7 Q11a; detail in `biome_rulings.md`.

## Facts you cannot guess

- **The game reads `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RimWorld\Mods`,
  never this repo.** Writing a file is not deploying it.
- **A cold load is ~15 minutes on the full list; a quicktest map is ~90 s.** Never
  "restart and see". *(MEASURED 2026-09-07, second launch of a session; a first launch
  after a reboot may run slower.)*
- **`ModsConfig.xml` is the live mod list**, at
  `C:\Users\Mandrake\AppData\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\Config\ModsConfig.xml`.
  🔴 **Parse it** (`ET.parse(p).find("activeMods")`) for the active count — never `grep` it,
  and never cite a mod count written in a doc. ModsConfig describes the NEXT load.
- 🔴 **Never restore the owner's mod list; only canonical world saves are precious** (owner, 2026-10-24):
  *"Never worry about my mod list restoration! … Until I start playing (months from now likely) you never need
  to "restore" mods to anything or worry about harming save games other than canonical world saves."* Leave
  ModsConfig on whatever tier serves the work; no "restore before release" step. Every save except the canonical
  world saves (`infrastructure/state/CANONICAL_SAVE.md`) is disposable.
- **Never guess a defName, field, or namespace.** RimSage (`mcp__rimsage__*`, Windows
  Desktop only), the def, the About.xml, or `measure` — and 🔴 **a number about a large
  artifact comes from `measure`, never from a scan** (`block_blind_scan.py` refuses).
  `0` means measured zero; ignorance answers `UNMEASURED`.
- 🔴 **Instrument-blindness is a user-level rule.** Measured traps here (ledger key is `id` not `item`, `python.exe` CRLF,
  `grep -c` exit 1, zsh no word-split, `ls|wc` on a missing dir, `*south*` mask glob, creature
  census by description not defName, "is there a mod for X" across BOTH mod roots incl.
  inactive …): `infrastructure/state/facts/instrument_traps.md`.
- 🔴 **`Plant` only ticks `TickLong()`** — a comp on a plant overrides `CompTickLong()`.
  🔴 **`MayRequire` on a top-level `<Operation>` is IGNORED** — guard with
  `PatchOperationFindMod`/`Conditional`; a composed member's packageId never loads. A patch
  that matches nothing logs nothing. Detail: `skills/rimworld-modding/references/project-engine-facts.md`.
- 🔴 **`modcheck run <Mod>` REWRITES the live `ModsConfig.xml`** (expensive list). When a new
  game won't start, read the **FIRST** exception in `Player.log`, not the loudest. More
  (600 s subagent watchdog, mid-session hooks, card gates, `handoff.py` and two Conductor
  windows): `infrastructure/state/facts/tool_traps.md`.
- **Dumps and harvests decay** (owner, 2026-08-27): trust one only after its fingerprint
  matches the live mod set; the frozen `official` dump is the sole design target.

## North-star validation — owner, 2026-09-17

The validated-hash covers the WHOLE `## north star` section, prose included. *"Change no code —
you just re-validate when prose is corrected."* So: correct false text, then re-validate on his
word the same sitting; write only state-independent prose there. Validation state is never
written as prose — `modcheck floor --all` measures it. Walk-finding traps and the rest:
`design/RimMandrake/standing_rulings.md`.

## In-game LLM access is the Claude Code CLI, never a hosted API key — owner, 2026-09-05

Every in-game LLM call shells out to **`claude -p "<prompt>"`** as a subprocess. Owner,
verbatim: *"Claude Code in non-interactive mode (`claude -p "..."`) authenticates via your
claude.ai login and can be called from a shell script without any API key."* The spec's two
laws (text/menu authority only; the game is whole with the LLM absent) stand. Detail:
`standing_rulings.md`; spec: `design/RimMandrake/llm_ingame_wiring_spec.md`.

## A pit is a SUPERDEEP cell, not a building — owner, 2026-09-17

*"I'm not really sure a pit is any different than a deep canal."* 🔴 **The ITEM
`infrastructure/state/items/PIT_SUPERDEEP_COLLAPSE_1.md` is the authority, not the 1127-line
spec**, which predates ten changed answers. Summary in `standing_rulings.md`.

## 🔴 One Direct Sun, a pure function of geometry — owner, 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-19

*"It can't be a new "kind" of heat."* · *"no biome-specific heat, no biome-specific sun. It's a matter
of geometry (low sun is less intense AND produces longer shade, high sun produces only covered shade
and much more intense effect). Ambient heat is normal Rimworld rules."* Direct Sun feeds **vanilla**
heat (felt temperature → Heatstroke), 55 °C at the zenith × sin(sun angle), the sun angle from the
tile's planet position; no per-biome heat kind, number or exception. Shade gear is parasols and roofs
(a tent is any quick roof). Volcanic/steam/fog heat is plain air temperature. And **no animal or pawn
ever vanishes without a readable sign.** 🔑 **Running it on every day-side map depends on tree
shade:** *"If we have an excellent tree shade model working, then YES direct sun works the same
everywhere on the day side."* Without one, it is turned off on tree-heavy maps, which he calls
inferior. The model: `design/RimMandrake/tree_shade_model_2026-10-19.md`. Full text:
`standing_rulings.md` §Direct Sun; design and migration:
`design/RimMandrake/unified_direct_sun_heat_2026-10-19.md`.

## 🔑 Every DLC is assumed — owner, 2026-09-19/25/26

- *"Always assume all the dlcs."* and *"it is assumed that future players will have all the
  Rimworld DLC's currently installed."* ⇒ **Every DLC is a hard prerequisite of shipping**, like
  the base game. ⛔ No DLC-less degradation path, no "what if the player lacks X" defect, no test
  tier proving a DLC-absent configuration. `MayRequire` stays on **mod** guards for load safety;
  on a DLC it decides nothing.
- **ALL TEST MOD LISTS include ALL FIVE EXPANSIONS** — *"ALL TEST MOD LISTS should include ALL
  THE EXPANSIONS; we're not trying to ablate expansions out of our list at this time."* A tier
  may narrow which mods load, never which DLC.

## Shipping names are three-tier — owner, 2026-08-30

Every NEW packageId, defName, C# namespace and mod folder follows `design/NAMING_SCHEME_PLAN.md`:
**RimMandrake** / **RimStarWars** / **RimUtinni** — packageId `mandrake.<tier>.<modname>`,
prefixes `RM_`/`RSW_`/`RUT_`, namespaces `RimMandrake[.StarWars|.Utinni].<Mod>`. "Jawa" is lore
text only; dev tooling is exempt. 🔴 **The migration is DONE** (*"Deploy the full rename."*,
2026-08-31) — a later rename is simply owed work; delete any doc still citing a rename gate.

## Sittings with the owner keep the advanced-zoom mod — owner, 2026-11-03

*"there was a standing rule that the advanced zoom capabilities were always to be included in mod lists where the human sat with Conductor, so I can zoom in and study things."* Any mod list built for a sitting with him includes it.

## Every mod ships superb Mod Settings — owner, 2026-09-12

On/off per major feature, tuning where a number is the experience, defaults = shipped
behaviour, all-off degrades gracefully, worldgen-affecting toggles labelled. Applies to every mod,
no exceptions. **Biome mechanics are promised inside OUR biomes only** (owner, 2026-10-15: *"We can't
guarantee they will work in other biomes beyond our framework. They should… but we're not going to
validate that at this time."*): build no new cross-biome switch; existing ones stay, off, labelled
unsupported.

## If it flies in the fiction, it flies in the game — owner, 2026-09-19

*"Standing rule: we make flyers flyers when we can, ok?"* Real flight, triggered by touching
the def, not a sweep. Flight is the **`MaxFlightTime` STAT** (Core, not a donor); the animation
is a **whole-body directional flip-book** (`flyingAnimationFramePathPrefix`), ⛔ never a Spastic
wing render-tree. Mechanics: `skills/rimworld-modding/references/flight.md`.

🔴🔴 **NEVER live-test a flyer's flight without the owner present** — *"For the third time, do
not do live testing of flyers without a human present. It doesn't work."* and *"Don't try to
capture images of flight. It doesn't work."* Verify flight by a deterministic STATE read of
`Pawn_FlightTracker`; a visual check is a joint session or it waits.

## Queue items are NAMED, not numbered

The grammar is `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s `PROJECT_VERB_INTENTION_TWIST`; this project's slot 1 for new names is `RIMMANDRAKE`.
The registry Id stays `rimmaster`; existing `RIMMASTER_*` names stay valid forever and are never renamed. `rimflow namecheck <NAME>`
shows the parse and `file`/`spawn` refuse the rest. The registry is read from `$LODESTAR_ROOT/sync/registry.md` (default `~/dev/Lodestar`);
if unreadable the refusal names that path. Older names (`SUBJECT_INTENT_TWIST`, `…_1`, `B*`/`C*`/`D*`/`W*`) stay valid forever, never
renamed. History: `design/RimMandrake/ticket_naming_2026-10-10.md`.

## Correctness outranks seat ownership; wrong material is deleted

User-level rule (fix a false statement on sight in anyone's file; delete, never supersede). Here: commit it at once by explicit path; full rule: CHARTER.

## 🔑 Agents decide nearly everything, art included — owner, 2026-10-22

*"Nearly everything including art. An agent can absolutely ask another agent for an art ruling based on some prose
constraints and requirements we can draft."* Taste calls go to a judge agent (not the maker); every delegated call is
logged `--why "delegated: <class>"`, never as his approval, and reaches him in a daily digest. Only the short list in
`design/RimMandrake/delegation_policy.md` §2 still needs him (north-star bars, irreversible acts on others' work,
replacing art he kept (except the art-eval pipeline's redraws, shown to him after with a revert — owner card

## The loop (seat)

```
./publish -m "subject" path/one path/two        # commit those paths, replay onto origin/main, push; prints PUBLISHED <sha>
land.sh <sha> <path>...                         # land one commit already made (any clone; plumbing)
land.sh -m "subject" <path>...                  # land working-tree bytes of the paths without a local commit
./sync                                          # realign this clone's main with origin/main (seat_sync.py)
```

- `./publish` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/publish.py`) commits by pathspec, re-creates any local commit not yet upstream on
  origin/main by plumbing (`merge-tree` + `commit-tree`), moves main there with `git reset --keep`, pushes, and retries up
  to 8 times when origin moved. It **never stashes**, so it works in a dirty clone: it refuses only on a real conflict or
  when you hold an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed, naming the path, with your commit intact on HEAD.
- `land.sh` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh`; `/home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh` is a one-line wrapper) publishes ONE
  commit or explicit paths by plumbing, retries a lost push race, then runs `./sync --no-fetch` itself. `LAND_REPO`
  defaults to the clone the cwd is in. stdout is exactly `PUBLISHED <sha>`; pass it to `rimflow close --sha`.
- `./sync` moves main to origin/main with `git reset --keep` only when every local commit is already upstream (git cherry
  `-`, or the same bytes per path) and no dirty file holds bytes other than upstream's; else it prints `REFUSED: <why>`
  and changes nothing. Local commits go to `backup/<seat>-pre-sync-<stamp>-<sha>`. Never stash, never `--hard`.
- Pathspec on the commit (`git commit <paths>`), never `git add -A`/`.`/`-a` (hook-enforced). Never `--force`. Never a file over ~50 MB.
- Proof of publication is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`, never an empty `git log origin/main..HEAD` and never the exit code: `./publish` can exit 120 with no output yet have pushed.
- Origin is SSH (`git@github.com:Lmandrake/RimMandrake.git`).
- Committed and pushed is the only durable state: commit at each finished unit and push at once.
- Do not `git pull --rebase` in a seat clone: it refuses on ANY dirty file, and a seat clone is always a little dirty.

## Traps

Each of these cost at least one lost or mis-published change. Most are hook-enforced or fixed in the tools above; the
rest are discipline.

| trap | what happens | do instead |
|---|---|---|
| `git add a b c 2>/dev/null` | one missing path fails the WHOLE add silently; the commit then runs on an empty or partial index and "succeeds" | never silence `git add`; check `git show --stat HEAD` |
| a deleted path on `git add` | `git add <deleted>` errors and kills the `&&` chain; the push after it says "Everything up-to-date" | put a deleted path on the commit pathspec only |
| pathspec commit takes the WORKTREE | `git commit <path>` is an implicit `git add` of that path: a blob you staged with `update-index` is ignored, and a peer's unsaved lines in the same file ride along | check `git diff --stat <path>` first; build partial commits in a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) |
| pathspec commit cannot remove-but-keep | `git rm --cached p` then `git commit p` re-adds `p` from the worktree | commit through a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=… git read-tree HEAD; git rm --cached …; write-tree; commit-tree`), then `git reset -q -- p` in the real index |
| untracked can't be pathspec-committed | `git commit <new file>` → "did not match any file(s) known to git"; a `git commit <dir>` silently skips new files in it | `git add -- <new file>` first (explicit path), then `git commit <paths>` |
| `-F -` after `--` | `git commit -- p -F -` treats `-F` and `-` as pathspecs | options before `--`, paths after |
| bare `git commit` | commits the WHOLE index, including what a helper staged in the same clone | always name paths (hook-enforced) |
| `.git/index.lock` exists | a background helper's read-only `git status` holds it for a second; a failed `./publish` then committed NONE of its paths | wait a few seconds and retry; never delete a lock younger than a minute; check `git status` after any failed publish |

- Rehearsing parallel integration: clone an integration repo with `-b main` (its HEAD may sit on the candidate branch mid fan-in); `git cherry-pick --continue` fails on an empty pick, use `--skip`; a board's `done` must mean LANDED before dependents are given.

# Delegation policy — agents decide nearly everything, art included

*Adopted 2026-10-22 on the owner's word (item `DELEGATION_POLICY_BUILD_AGENTS_ASK_AGENTS`). Binds BENCH,
Relentless and every subagent. Model tiers are `infrastructure/agents/Agent_Policy.md`'s, never restated here.*

## The ruling

Owner, 2026-10-22 ~16:05 PDT, answering *"Which decisions may agents take without asking you?"*:

> *"Nearly everything including art. An agent can absolutely ask another agent for an art ruling based on
> some prose constraints and requirements we can draft. It would catch most of what we look for anyway. Then
> we would do a review from a much stronger place. Art already takes many passes even with a human in the
> loop."*

The card option he chose the spirit of was *"Nearly everything, with timeouts — all but art, north-star bars
and anything irreversible"*; he explicitly extended it to art. This replaces the 2026-09-15 rule *"Cosmetic
changes need his permission first"* and the habit of putting taste calls to him by card before acting.

**Why:** his minutes go where only he can judge, and he judges from a pre-filtered set instead of raw output.
**What it does NOT change:** his standing rulings. Delegation acts *inside* them, never over them (§2.4).

## 1. What agents now decide alone

Everything not on the §2 list. That includes, and is not limited to:

| class (the `<class>` in the log line) | examples |
|---|---|
| `technical` | harness thresholds, test-site choice, refactors inside a mod, MOD/SITE/HARNESS calls with evidence, tool design |
| `scope` | splitting, narrowing, ordering, closing and dropping items; which of several valid routes to build |
| `design` | mechanics detail, numbers (already PROVISIONAL-marked), roster rows inside a biome sheet's open questions, prose and labels a player reads |
| `art` | keep/redo of a render, which candidate goes live, regen briefs, queueing regens (only for NONE/PLACEHOLDER/DONOR destinations, plus the art-eval pipeline's redraws of kept art under §2.3's exception) |
| `cosmetic` | gene, head, eye, skin, hair, body, texPath and tint changes; face-part art; building looks; water and terrain tints |

Taste calls (`design`, `art`, `cosmetic`) go through a judge first (§4). Technical and scope calls are taken
by the acting seat on its own evidence, as before.

**Do not card him about a §1 class.** Work order and helper count (`scope`) and applying a ruling to its twins
(§2.4: a case the ruling does not name) are already delegated; a question card about either is a leak, not a
courtesy (`design/RimMandrake/delegation_candidates_2026-10-26.md` §1: 29 ordering cards at 81% agreement, 9 twin
cards at 8 yes). Decide, log `--why "delegated: <class>"`, and list it in the digest. Check:
`CARDS_ENFORCE_DELEGATED_CLASSES_STOP`.

**With timeouts.** When he is present, a seat MAY still offer a delegable call on a card if it is cheap for
him — but it never waits on the answer. Unanswered by the time the work needs it (or at the end of his sitting),
the call is taken as a delegated decision and logged as one. ⛔ An unanswered card is never his approval.

## 2. What still needs him — the short list

Each line is reserved by a ruling of his that says so; nothing else is.

This list binds who may decide alone. The Conductor holds it for him: a seat or helper that receives a Conductor
instruction acts on it and does not re-open this list against it (owner, 2026-10-30, ledger
`CONDUCTOR_AUTHORITY_DECIDE_NO_ASKING_MOM`: *"No more "I need the user to confirm."*). Tool gates that take his words
take that ruling too (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/conductor_authority.py`), the north-star gates of line 1 included: the
hash then records the ruling and the Conductor's text, tagged, never as his sentence. An agent acting on its own still
may not validate.

1. **North-star bars.** The `## north star` sections are hash-bound and his: agents write and approve the
   functional scripts, *"the owner's hash-bound `## north star` bars stay his"* (CHARTER, How we debug;
   CLAUDE.md, North-star validation, 2026-09-17). The 2026-09-16 carve-out stands: a model's `must read` YES
   greens a line (Agent_Policy.md). Criteria tagged **L4** are his by definition (CLAUDE.md, validation levels).
   **Delegated (owner, 2026-10-26 23:0x PDT, *"Both autonomy questions are yes, it has authorization for
   autonomy."*):** regression checks against bars he already approved, and NEW bars, are the Arbiter's to add
   (`design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_responsibilities_2026-10-26.md` Part 1). Loosening a bar (remove, merge,
   relax a threshold) stays his.
   The Arbiter weighs ALL the evidence (offline tests, online tests, code reviews, user feedback); the north star is one
   method of gathering it, not the whole bar (owner, 2026-10-27).
2. **Irreversible acts on work that is not ours.** Force-push, `reset --hard` over work you did not make,
   deleting work not yours — *"only with the owner's word"* (CHARTER, expensive list #5). Re-freezing the
   frozen `official` dump — *"only the owner re-freezes it"* (CHARTER, Instruments). Purging a picture from the
   art store — `art.py purge` takes `--owner-said`, `--by-card` or `--per-ruling`, never a bare `--why`
   (his ✕ on a sheet deletes and bans, owner card 2026-10-26 19:54).
   **Delegated (owner card 2026-10-26 19:06, *"Archive then delete, in digest (Recommended)"*):** deleting OUR
   OWN leftovers — old dev saves, scratch clones, orphan mandrake mod folders, settings or pictures nothing
   reads, patches aimed at retired mods — when a check proves nothing reads it AND everything is pushed, after
   archiving or bundling it under agent storage (`D:\ClaudeWork`), with each deletion listed in his daily
   digest. Ruled words: *"May agents delete our own leftovers when a check proves nothing reads them and
   everything is pushed, after archiving or bundling them, and list each in your digest?"* Checker:
   `LEFTOVERS_BUILD_ARCHIVE_THEN_DELETE`. Anything not ours, or not proven unread and pushed, is still his.
3. **Replacing art he KEPT** — with ONE exception. *"Why are we replacing items for which I know I have good
   versions?"* (2026-10-19). `art.py install --reason` refuses over an owner-kept picture; a delegated call never
   works around that refusal. **Exception (owner card 2026-10-23 06:42, *"Yes, but show me after"*):** the art-eval
   pipeline (`skills/rimworld-art-evaluation`) MAY redraw a kept picture when its verdict is regen (Opus really
   bad, or a weak one GPT did not strong-accept), only with a revert record, installing through
   `art.py install --by-card "Kept art judged really bad: may the pipeline redraw it on its own? → Yes, but show me after"`; every such swap appears on the next shadow sheet flagged
   *replaced your kept art* with a one-click revert to the kept version through the art ledger.
   **Second exception (owner card 2026-10-26 18:46, *"Yes, delegate this class"*):** a *geometric correction* of
   existing art, kept or not — moving, aligning or trimming pixels, with no new drawing and no change of style or
   colour — MAY be installed without him when a player-truth check measures the defect before and confirms it gone
   after. It is judged by an agent that did not make it, logged `--why "delegated: art geometric correction"`,
   installed through `art.py install --by-card "To make the system more fire-and-forget, may I decide this class of
   art change without you from now on? → Yes, delegate this class (Recommended)"` (old bytes archived, one-command
   revert), and listed in his daily digest after the fact. First use: the pipe elbow seams (PIPE_ELBOW_FIX_SEAM_JOGS).
   **Third exception (owner cards 2026-10-26 19:06 and 19:54):** his own sheet marks are carried out without
   asking him again. When his newer mark conflicts with an older keep, the newest mark wins (19:06, *"Newest mark
   wins"*). **His ✕ deletes the picture forever and bans it** (19:54, *"X = delete forever + ban"*, on the card
   "You want an X to delete a picture permanently so it never returns … What should X mean now?"): the bytes are
   purged from the art store and a permanent ban record (exact sha + near-duplicates by visual similarity) is
   checked by every sheet build, every install and every redraw, so an ✕'d picture never returns by any route.
   Each act is listed in his daily digest. Tooling: `art.py enact` applies newest-mark-wins (each act carries his
   mark: sheet, row, click time, `why "delegated: art marks"`); the ✕ is carried out by `artledger.x_delete`
   (file + store bytes removed, `ban` recorded) and the ban is enforced by `art_sheet` / `sheet_to_artifact`,
   `install` / `install_bytes`, artpipe (discard + re-roll, `ban_hit`) and art_eval (regen); only
   `art.py unban <sha> --owner-said "…"` lifts it (`ART_X_BUILD_DELETE_FOREVER_BAN`). Leftover pictures that he did NOT ✕ follow the cleanup ruling (§2.2:
   archive, then delete) — only his ✕ means forever.
   Any other replacement of kept art is still his.
4. **Overturning or reinterpreting a standing ruling of his** — CLAUDE.md, `standing_rulings.md`,
   `biome_rulings.md`, a canon entry's `## ruling` (*"The ruling is his, never yours"*, `AGENT_BRIEF.md`), and
   deliberate departures from canon. Applying a ruling to a case it does not name is delegated; changing what
   it says is not.
5. **Outward and paid acts.** Spending money, publishing outside our private repos and artifacts (a Steam
   Workshop upload, a public post), and the acts his global instructions call his: an interactive login, a
   GUI he must look at, a purchase (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, "RUN IT YOURSELF" ③).
6. **Presence-bound acts his rulings name.** Live flight tests of a flyer — *"do not do live testing of flyers
   without a human present"* (CLAUDE.md, flight); `broadcast.py` is his; `./bridge bench|foundry|free` is his
   except as delegated here. **Delegated:** a seat MAY take the bridge, deploy and restart the game on its own
   when the bridge is free, ours, or stale by the 45-minute rule, his OWNER hold only 45 min after his last interaction (owner card 2026-10-30), and never for a flyer's
   flight. Each take and restart is listed in his daily digest. His presence at the machine plays no part (owner,
   2026-10-30, verbatim: *"I really, really need you to strip "when I come back to the machine" as an event for anything changing. It's causing so many problems and I don't need it."*): nothing reads his input clock. Tooling: `rimflow bridge idle` reports TAKEABLE or

   refusal is self-declared: `--flyer` and any purpose that names flying refuse, but the tool cannot know what the
   seat will actually drive. A seat that will fly anything passes `--flyer`.
7. **Certifying a mod's first-touch Designer pass.** *"the first time an item names a mod, it gets a deep Designer
   pass to read out its code/spec, expand the spec and validation strategies, certifies it with the user/clarifies
   confusion, then writes it all out for Relentless."* (owner, 2026-11-04 UTC, ledger `FIRST_TOUCH_BUILD_DESIGNER_READS_FIRST`;

   Designer's; only the certification sitting with him is reserved. One item per mod (`<FOLDER>_DESIGN_FIRST_TOUCH`):
   each sitting certifies a different spec, so no one ruling settles the family. System-class items (Operations' system set) are
   exempt from the first-touch hold (owner card 2026-11-05, "Let all system work through"): repairs do not change what a mod is;

A reserved call is asked as a card (the `question-card` skill) or filed `--for OWNER --kind decision`, and the
work waits on it. It never times out into a decision.

## 3. How a delegated decision is recorded

- **Ledger:** `rimflow note <ID> --why "delegated: <class>" --text "<the decision; judge verdict file if any>"`
  (or the same `--why` on `close`/`drop`/`supersede`/`file`). ⛔ Never `--owner-said`, `--by-card` or
  `--per-ruling` — those name his authority; this ruling authorises the *class*, the call itself is ours.
- **Commit:** a body line `Delegated: <class> — <one-line decision>` so `git log --grep '^Delegated:'` finds it.
- **Art install:** `art.py install … --why "delegated: art <verdict file>"` (`--why` grants no owner authority: the mechanical guards apply, so it never displaces a kept, purged or rejected picture; `--reason` takes only mechanical tags and refuses this text). The pre-push `art_guard` accepts it when the verdict file exists in the clone (`ART_GUARD_FIX_REFUSES_THE_DELEGATE`).
- **Verdicts:** the judge's output (§4) is committed as
  `infrastructure/state/delegated/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<subject-or-item>.json` and cited by path.
- **Numbers and rosters in `canon.yml`:** a delegated value carries `src: delegated:<class> (<item>)`, never a
  quote of his.

## 4. Asking another agent — the judge protocol

1. **A different agent decides.** The maker never judges its own output. The judge is a fresh subagent spawned
   for the call, with no maker context: it sees only the artifact(s), the written constraints, and the question.
2. **Model per `Agent_Policy.md`.** Art, the world and any call no later check catches sit on its opus rows.
3. **The brief is written, not remembered.** Art and cosmetic calls: `design/RimMandrake/art_judge_brief.md`
   plus the subject's canon entry (`## Must show`, `## Engine limits`) if it has one. Design calls: the item's
   criteria, the governing design doc, and every standing ruling it touches, quoted.
4. **The judge returns keep/redo with reasons** — per artifact `KEEP` or `REDO`, each REDO quoting the violated
   constraint and its source, plus `UNSURE` when the written constraints do not decide it (the brief's format).
5. **The maker does not overrule a REDO.** It may re-ask a *new* judge once with a written rebuttal; the second
   verdict stands. Two UNSUREs, or a subject still REDO after three rounds, goes to his set flagged (§6).
6. **A judge's miss is a brief defect.** When he overturns a KEEP, the reason becomes a new line in the brief
   (with his words as its source), the same day.

## 5. How he audits and overturns cheaply — the daily digest

Once a day, before the Conductor's first scheduled check, a program writes
`Transient/delegated_digest_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` and the Conductor gives him its full native path: one line per delegated call
since the last digest — item, class, decision, judge verdict file — newest first, art grouped by subject. Built
by a program, `src/RimMandrake/rimflow/delegated_digest.py` (the Conductor's scheduled pre-step; token-blind by
allow-list), from the ledger (`why` starting `delegated:`), `git log --grep '^Delegated:'`, the judge records in
`infrastructure/state/delegated/`, the art ledger's delegated installs and marks, and the leftovers acts log; a zero-line digest is checked
against a known delegated event before it is reported as zero. Every act under the 2026-10-26 card delegations is
a digest line: each newest-mark enactment, ✕ delete + ban, ban lifted, and redraw a ban discarded (§2.3, class
`art marks`; `art.py marks-digest` lists them), each bridge take, deploy and
restart (§2.6, class `bridge idle`), each leftover deleted with its archive or bundle path (§2.2, class
`leftovers`) — logged `--why "delegated: <class>"` so the digest finds it.
The same page lists every open item on the OWNER seat at its cut, oldest first, with its age since filed and how many
open items wait on it (direct: a live block names it; chain: a chain of live blocks reaches it) — visibility only, no
default applied or recommended (D4(a), `OWNER_ASKS_MEASURE_AGE_IN_DIGEST`; revisit a default only after two weeks of
age data).

To overturn: he says so, in any words; the seat records his words with `--owner-said` on the item, undoes the
call, and adds the reason to the brief (§4.6). Silence on a digest line is not his approval — it stays logged as
delegated.

## 6. What reaches him — the review "from a much stronger place"

He reviews a **curated, pre-judged set**, never raw output (and nothing reaches him unread — `standing_rulings.md`
§Nothing reaches the owner unread, owner 2026-10-22; a sheet carries its `<stem>.prereview.json`): only judge-KEEP art (with the verdict lines beside
each picture), plus rows flagged *split* (two UNSUREs), *stuck* (three REDO rounds), *kept-but-flagged* or *replaced your kept art* (§2.3).
It reaches him the ways he already reviews — a review sheet that is truly new and passes its gates
(`rimworld-review-sheets`), a phone set (full-res alone, true scale, facings), or an in-game review map for
visuals judged by looking — never a sheet of REDOs. Delegated art may be installed before his review; biome art
never blocks (`standing_rulings.md`, 2026-10-18). His ruling there is recorded as his (`--owner-said`) and
makes the picture owner-kept.

# CHARTER — binds the Conductor and Relentless

*Adopted 2026-08-27 (owner's ruling, this date), replacing POLICY.md, the four seat
files, and most of the process prose. Git holds everything removed. **This file does
not grow: a new line must delete the line it replaces.***

## Posture

**Act first.** Anything git can undo — edits, deletes, renames, docs, queue items —
gets no verification, no filing, no report beyond one line: do it, commit explicit
paths, push, "Done, `<hash>`." The owner's word closes, opens, or overrides anything,
instantly and without re-derivation; when he says a thing is validated, it is. He is
never refused by a tool rule — find the flag or override (`--owner-said "<his
words>"`), run it yourself, and never hand him a command to paste. When he is present
you are at his side: do what he says, ask questions the moment they exist. He opts
work *into* rigor ("careful with this one"), never out of it.

**See it, fix it, then** (owner, 2026-11-05: *"if you know what's wrong and it's easy to fix, it should NOT just be
"added to the ticket and wait." That's old foundry behavior. If you see something, fix it RIGHT THEN, ok? Standing
policy."*). Every seat and helper: a known, small fix (a proof argument, a live line, a timeout, a packageId, a
worded criterion, an unanswered hold whose answer exists) is made on the spot, published, and then the fixer runs the item's remaining check itself and closes it; the item goes
back to Relentless only if real build work remains, never for one more generation just to re-check (owner, 2026-11-05).
A diagnosis is never written onto a ticket in place of the fix. A ticket is filed only for what is not small, and it says why. And the pipeline never "blesses" a small change (owner, 2026-11-05): a quick manual validation is done by the
agent on the spot and closed with that evidence, never queued for a Judge (`standing_rulings.md`).

## The expensive list — the only things that get ceremony

1. **A cold-load slot** (~15 min on the full list, MEASURED 2026-09-07). Batch questions; write the Player.log strings that
   will decide each before launch (`rimworld-load-round`).
2. **`deploy_custom_mods.py --apply`** — read the plan first; never deploy over
   another window's uncommitted files.
3. **`ModsConfig.xml` writes** (`rimworld-start-prep`). Unattended mod-list
   experiments: snapshot to `infrastructure/state/modlists/`, sweep dependents,
   announce loudly where he reads.
4. **Savegame writes** to the frozen world or ship saves — back up first
   (`rimworld-savegame`).
5. **History and others' work** — force-push, `reset --hard` over work you did not make,
   deleting work not yours: warn in one line, then only with the owner's word. Our own
   proven-unread, pushed leftovers: archive, delete, digest (`delegation_policy.md` §2.2).
6. **Anything the owner must LOOK at** — read by us first, every item an agent can judge, broken ones fixed or
   dropped (owner, 2026-10-22; `standing_rulings.md` §Nothing reaches the owner unread), then given with the
   complete native path in backticks, spaces as spaces.

Ceremony means: the one pre-check the tool names, evidence in the closing commit,
spec/verify prose only here. Everything not on this list — including maps, saves,
colonies and deployed mod folders outside the repo — is not precious; the repo is the
protected thing.

## Git

CLAUDE.md owns the rules ("Git" + the Transient rule); `design/RimMandrake/GIT_WORKFLOW.md`
is the operating doc. Charter's additions only: commit when a unit of work exists, and work
only in your seat clone (`/home/mandrake/rm/<seat>`) — `D:\Luke\dev\RimMandrake` is a
read-only mirror.

Worktrees are OFF and helpers write in the window's clone: CLAUDE.md "Git" and `Agent_Policy.md` "Helpers in this repo".

## Queue

An item is one line — `SUBJECT_INTENT_TWIST · lane · the ask` (grammar: `design/RimMandrake/ticket_naming_2026-10-10.md`) — plus optional
prose in `infrastructure/state/items/<ID>.md` for expensive-list items only. 🔑 **On
close/drop/supersede the prose moves to `items/closed/<ID>.md`** — so `items/*.md` is
the LIVE set and a sweep stops walking finished work; `rimflow show` resolves both.
Reboot handoffs are not items and live in `infrastructure/state/handoffs/`. The
ledger — the frozen `events.jsonl` plus one `ledger/events/<SEAT>.jsonl` shard per
seat since 2026-09-23, written only by `rimflow` — is the truth; `queue/<SEAT>.md` files are
gitignored rendered views you never edit — read one with `rimflow queue <SEAT>`, which
renders first (`queue/HUMAN.md` is the owner's hand-written inbox and stays tracked). Close: `rimflow close <ID> --sha <commit>`, commit
carrying `Closes: <ID>`, push.

🔴 **RELENTLESS BUILDS AND ACCEPTS EVERYTHING, FLOWWORKS AND GSS INCLUDED; FOUNDRY IS RETIRED — owner, by card 2026-11-02** (`CLAUDE.md`). The Conductor's window takes only an item that needs him live (needs=owner, an L4 look, flyer live tests). A FlowWorks finding is filed `--for CONDUCTOR` (written RELENTLESS, the builder that takes it); lane data: `infrastructure/state/flowworks_lane.json`.

🔴 **ANY SEAT ENDS AN ITEM IT FINDS DEAD — owner's ruling, 2026-09-19.** The moment
any seat finds a queue item **completed, totally invalidated, superseded, or otherwise
no longer worth considering for activity**, that seat ends it itself — no routing to
the owning seat, no `--owner-said`, no asking. Ownership gates work in flight
(`claim`, `start`, `block`, `verify`, `reclaim`, `renew`, `release`, `implemented`, `reconcile`),
never the three terminal verbs. `implemented` is not terminal: it records published code and the
level-tagged criteria still owed (`built` -> `validated` -> `done`); only `done`, `drop` and
`supersede` end an item:

```
rimflow close <ID> --sha <commit> --reason "<what proves it done>"
rimflow drop  <ID> --reason "<what proves it dead>"
rimflow supersede <ID> --by <NEW_ID> --reason "<why the successor replaces it>"
```

The ledger event stamps the **ruling seat** automatically — that is the record of who
called it, and `--reason` is the ruling itself, mandatory in practice on another seat's
item. ⛔ **The evidence bar is unchanged**: done means proven, dead means probed. This
removed the seat boundary, not the requirement to have looked. **Stale default:** one
grep/probe — if it doesn't prove the item live, `rimflow drop <ID> --reason
"stale-drop: <the probe>"`; real work re-files itself. Naming: CLAUDE.md's "Queue items are NAMED" section. Helpers, lanes and groupings are named too, never coded: no C6, A5 or "Lane A2" (they collide with legacy ledger ids; hook `block_agent_coded_name.py`). v2 ideas
go straight to `design/V2_DREAMS.md`, any window, no permission.

## Done means running — owner, 2026-10-31

An operational item (hook, unit, timer, ops rule, alarm) is done only when it names what must stay alive and its last
reading: close with `--live "unit=… reading=… max_age=…"`. `rimflow` refuses an unproven close, and `rm-deadman`
reopens the same item if it dies. CLAUDE.md "An operational item is done only when it is running"; full text
`design/RimMandrake/parallel_review_2026-10-31/folded_into_operations.md`.

## Correctness outranks seat ownership — owner, 2026-09-19

> *"It is WORSE to leave incorrect information that belongs to another seat than it is
> to violate seats... ok? I keep saying this. MAKE IT SO EVERYWHERE."*

🔴 **Find a false statement in another seat's file — item prose, spec, doc — and you
FIX IT. Now, yourself.** Not a correction item, not a note, not a message. The seat
boundary never protected a wrong sentence, and every reader downstream believes it
until someone crosses the line.

- **Commit it immediately, by explicit path.** The real risk was never the crossing —
  it was an uncommitted fix sitting in a tree four threads share, erased by the next
  checkout with nobody told. Committing IS the safeguard.
- **Say what was WRONG in the commit, not just what you changed.** The owning seat
  reads the log, not your reasoning.
- ⛔ **Fixing ≠ redirecting.** Scope, priorities and decisions stay theirs: correct
  what is FALSE, and `rimflow file --for <them>` anything that is a judgement call.
- `queue_lint.py` enforces exactly this: a cross-seat item edit WARNS and never
  refuses (48/48 selftests). Deleting wrong content beats annotating it — see
  CLAUDE.md's "Correctness outranks seat ownership; wrong material is deleted".

## 🔴 The Conductor speaks with the owner's authority — owner, 2026-10-30

CLAUDE.md's section of that name is the rule: an instruction from the Conductor carries his authority for every seat and helper
(Relentless, Dispatcher, Operations, RUNNER, subagents); never ask him to confirm one. Ledger: `--per-ruling CONDUCTOR_AUTHORITY_DECIDE_NO_ASKING_MOM`
plus the Conductor's text in `--why`.

## Decisions

Agents decide nearly everything, art included (owner, 2026-10-22); only
`design/RimMandrake/delegation_policy.md` §2 still needs him. Taste calls go to a judge agent, every
delegated call is logged `--why "delegated: <class>"` and reaches him in a daily digest. A ruling is one
dated line in `infrastructure/state/canon.yml` (numbers, rosters — every value with a `src:`) or on the item (scope). A reversal
**replaces** the old line in the same commit and propagates to every file naming the
item, same commit. A ruling under 24 h old is a draft — reversible without ceremony.

## Rules and lessons

An enforced rule is a **hook** (`.claude/hooks/`); propose the hook, not a paragraph.
A default worth stating is a **line in this charter**, replacing one. Everything else
is deleted — git is the archive. Lessons: one file each into
`infrastructure/state/lessons/` (`python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/lessons.py add "…"`), at any time and at reboot; skills are edited
only in a fresh-context curation session, never at end-of-context. A fact that
outgrows its doc goes to `infrastructure/state/facts/` — unbudgeted, never dropped
for space.

## Instruments, in order — and dumps decay

**RimSage** (`mcp__rimsage__*`: defs + engine C#, no load) → **`measure`/the def
dump** (post-patch truth; never a bare number from a scan — `MEASURED`/`UNMEASURED`/
`REFUSED`) → **quicktest via bridge** (~90 s) → **cold load** (expensive list).
**Be suspicious of every dump and harvest: it answers only for the mod set and moment
it captured.** Check currency by fingerprint, never timestamp; the frozen `official`
dump is the design target and only the owner re-freezes it. The silent-failure traps
(patches, deploys, defName guessing) are CLAUDE.md's "Facts you cannot guess".

Which kind of testing to run, and when, and its tunables: `design/RimMandrake/testing_policy_2026-10-28.md` and `src/RimMandrake/rimflow/testing_policy.json` (owner, 2026-10-28: "Let's get smarter about the testing we do and only use appropriate kinds of testing when/where it will help us.").

## How we debug — owner, 2026-10-01

`design/RimMandrake/debug_process.md` is the process. **Every mod has a functional script
and is debugged through it**: run it first, poke live when it is blind, and end every
poking session by writing the lesson into the script — a check red for the reported
reason before the final fix, plus the informative theories that proved false. Agents
write, approve and declare passing on these scripts; they may add regression checks and
new `## north star` bars (owner 2026-10-26, `delegation_policy.md` §2.1); loosening a bar stays his. Stuck → GPT early, for hypotheses to test.
**3 non-pass runs in a row, or a defect that needs live observation, goes to a Test Pilot, not another retest**
(owner 2026-10-31; `rimflow pilot`, `.claude/agents/rm-testpilot.md`, `standing_rulings.md`).

The 2026-10-01 build pause was lifted by the owner 2026-10-02 (*"Build pause is lifted."*);
every new mod still ships with its first script (`debug_process.md` §2).

## Game state and the bridge

He says it, you run it: `./game --said "<his words>" up|down|loading`. A restart you call
yourself: `./game --why "<your reason>" <state>` — never `--said`. Ledger provenance, one field per kind of authority: CLAUDE.md "Owner authority on the ledger".
Never infer state; bare `./game` measures and corrects the ledger, any window.
`broadcast.py` is his, with that single carve-out — and the carve-out is STAMP-ONLY
(owner, 2026-09-29): a seat's relay writes the ledger and messages no window; peers
read the state from `rimflow next`, which measures the game itself. The bridge is
one driver at a time — `rimflow bridge take` / `release`; CLAUDE.md's "The bridge is
passed through one file" is canonical (a free bridge is takeable; his machine use gates nothing — never flyer flight; `delegation_policy.md` §2.6). Config files
(`ModsConfig.xml` included) never wait for RimSort or the game; only assemblies need
the game down (OS lock).

## Windows

**the Conductor** (with the owner; `CONDUCTOR.md`) and **Relentless** (the Relentless Pipeline, the autonomous builder, no window; `src/RimMandrake/rimflow/relentless.py`; its places hold Relentless-style Builder/Judge workers from MandrakeWorkflows, `rm-builder` and `rm-judge`, swappable while the pipeline keeps its design: owner, 2026-11-03); every model choice, seat and subagent alike:
`Agent_Policy.md`. Subagents: spawn freely, always with `model`; a subagent's return
is evidence, never a finding, and no subagent writes shared state. Queue views render on every `rimflow` write — no loop, no
publisher, no staleness.

**Rebooting a window is prepared, not improvised** (owner, 2026-09-06). At a real
wave boundary — subagents all reported, everything committed and pushed, nothing
mid-edit — and above all the moment you would say *"that's all I have for now"*,
write the handoff with `RIMFLOW_SEAT=<SEAT> python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/handoff.py`
(the env var is required on any machine without a seat profile; it REFUSES rather than guess), fill
the four sections it leaves marked (it lands `conversations/` itself; `--check` refuses while a record is
uncommitted — owner 2026-10-18), pass `--check`, then say **HANDOFF READY** as
your last line and start nothing new. The phrase is the signal, and only a seat may say it — the script refuses to.
On a seat with a restart the phrase fires it: the Stop hook `.claude/hooks/handoff_restart.py` requests the
restart and the Dispatcher relaunches the window 20 s after its helpers finish (owner, 2026-11-01: "20 seconds, build it
now and implement."). The Conductor's window closes on his goodbye instead, and otherwise he reboots on his own clock.
Say it **once**: until real work comes in, `handoff.py` reports ALREADY HANDED OFF
and writes nothing, because a signal given every idle turn is not a signal.
# Git workflow — the operating doc (2026-10-02)

Rationale and measurements: `git_workflow_plan_2026-10-01.md` (plan) and the dated
`git_migration_*_2026-10-02.md` records (what was built). This file states what IS.

## Where work happens

| place | what it is |
|---|---|
| `/home/mandrake/rm/bench` | the seat clone — ext4, plain git, **one writer** (the seat's own window). The seat launches from its clone. (FOUNDRY is retired and its clone is deleted.) |
| `D:\Luke\dev\RimMandrake` (`/mnt/d/Luke/dev/RimMandrake`) | **read-only mirror** of origin/main, refreshed every 5 min by `rm-mirror.timer` (`./mirror sync`). No `.git`. Never write it; Windows tools (the game deploy, Explorer, python.exe) read it. `MIRROR_HEAD` names its commit; `MIRROR_STALE` appears if a refresh failed. |
| `/home/mandrake/rm/mirror.git` | the mirror's bare fetch-only repo |
| `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\artpipe\` | artpipe queue/state (not in git): `pending/ active/ done/ failed/ _artsrc/ registry.jsonl` |
| `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\build\`, `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\scratch\codex\` | build staging and codex.exe staging (drive-local scratch) |
| `/home/mandrake/rm/store.git` | the shared object store: bare, fetched from `mirror.git`, never pruned. Throwaway clones borrow from it, never from a seat clone |
| `/home/mandrake/rm/scratch/<SEAT>/` | throwaway ext4 clones, made only with `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/scratch_clone.py clone "<purpose>" [--sparse <dirs the task needs>]` (never `/tmp`: tmpfs). The default is a cone-sparse tree (root files, `.claude`, `infrastructure`, `skills`, `src/RimMandrake/Utils`, `src/RimMandrake/rimflow`, ~200 MB), not the whole ~4 GB; `--checkout` only for repo-wide work, say why in the purpose. Trial with telemetry: `design/RimMandrake/objstore_trial_2026-10-08.md` |

A session in the `D:\` mirror cannot commit: `./publish` refuses under `/mnt/`, and the
`block_shared_tree_merge.py` hook refuses whole-tree git there.

## The loop (seat)

```
./publish -m "subject" path/one path/two        # commit those paths, replay onto origin/main, push; prints PUBLISHED <sha>
land.sh <sha> <path>...                         # land one commit already made (any clone; plumbing)
land.sh -m "subject" <path>...                  # land working-tree bytes of the paths without a local commit
./sync                                          # realign this clone's main with origin/main (seat_sync.py)
```

- `./publish` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/publish.py`) commits by pathspec, re-creates any local commit not yet upstream on
  origin/main by plumbing (`merge-tree` + `commit-tree`), moves main there with `git reset --keep`, pushes, and retries up
  to 8 times when origin moved. It **never stashes**, so it works in a dirty clone: it refuses only on a real conflict or
  when you hold an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed, naming the path, with your commit intact on HEAD.
- `land.sh` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh`; `/home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh` is a one-line wrapper) publishes ONE
  commit or explicit paths by plumbing, retries a lost push race, then runs `./sync --no-fetch` itself. `LAND_REPO`
  defaults to the clone the cwd is in. stdout is exactly `PUBLISHED <sha>`; pass it to `rimflow close --sha`.
- `./sync` moves main to origin/main with `git reset --keep` only when every local commit is already upstream (git cherry
  `-`, or the same bytes per path) and no dirty file holds bytes other than upstream's; else it prints `REFUSED: <why>`
  and changes nothing. Local commits go to `backup/<seat>-pre-sync-<stamp>-<sha>`. Never stash, never `--hard`.
- Pathspec on the commit (`git commit <paths>`), never `git add -A`/`.`/`-a` (hook-enforced). Never `--force`. Never a file over ~50 MB.
- Proof of publication is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`, never an empty `git log origin/main..HEAD` and never the exit code: `./publish` can exit 120 with no output yet have pushed.
- Origin is SSH (`git@github.com:Lmandrake/RimMandrake.git`).
- Committed and pushed is the only durable state: commit at each finished unit and push at once.
- Do not `git pull --rebase` in a seat clone: it refuses on ANY dirty file, and a seat clone is always a little dirty.

## Subagents

- 🔴 **Worktrees are OFF** (owner, 2026-10-02, by card). Never `isolation: "worktree"`, never `git worktree add`; `.claude/hooks/block_worktrees.py` refuses both and the WorktreeCreate hook refuses `claude --worktree`. Why: worktree agents duplicated whole checkouts and stranded work on side branches.
- A writing helper edits in its window's clone; the window commits explicit paths with `./publish`. Writing helpers run one at a time when their paths could overlap.
- Brief helpers: `reset --hard`, `checkout --`, `stash` on paths they did not create are forbidden; a conflict is reported, never cleared.
- The drained worktree work is under `archive/*` tags on origin (`git checkout <tag> -- <path>` restores a file); `design/RimMandrake/git_migration_drain_2026-10-02.md` is the census.
- A helper must never rewrite commits it did not author. A guard refusal (e.g. the art push guard refusing deletion of owner-kept PNGs) is reported back and the parent lands it; one rm-fixer rewrote four unpublished local commits in the shared clone, one a peer's, to drop the deletions (trees matched, nothing lost, but never again).

## Generated and per-writer state (nothing shared to conflict on)

Each of these cost at least one lost or mis-published change. Most are hook-enforced or fixed in the tools above; the
rest are discipline.

| a deleted path on `git add` | `git add <deleted>` errors and kills the `&&` chain; the push after it says "Everything up-to-date" | put a deleted path on the commit pathspec only |
| pathspec commit takes the WORKTREE | `git commit <path>` is an implicit `git add` of that path: a blob you staged with `update-index` is ignored, and a peer's unsaved lines in the same file ride along | check `git diff --stat <path>` first; build partial commits in a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) |

# RimWorld modding

Patches fail *silently*, XML comments have a syntax rule most people don't know,
and a single bad Def entry can kill three unrelated mods at startup with an error
that names none of them. Almost every hour lost here is lost to writing something
plausible instead of reading something real.

The method: **find the ground truth on disk, write the smallest change that
survives a mod being absent, prove it before shipping, and record what you
learned.**

---

## 1. Read the real file first. Always.

Before writing a line of a patch, open the def you are patching and the def you
are patching *around* — the actual XML in the actual mod folder that is loaded
right now, not the wiki's version and not what a project doc said last month.

→ the grep command: `references/traps-xml-and-defs.md`.

This costs thirty seconds. Three specific reasons it matters more here than
elsewhere:

- **A failed PatchOperation is a no-op, not an error you'll notice.** It prints
  one line into a log with thousands of lines. Nothing breaks. The patch just
  never happened. You will believe it worked.
- **Def names are redefined by other mods.** The `Armadillo` you're looking at
  in Core may not be the `Armadillo` that wins. Last loaded def with a given
  `defName` replaces earlier ones entirely.
- **Fields move between versions.** `<wildness>` was valid on `RaceProperties`
  and isn't in 1.6. Read `XML error: <field> doesn't correspond to any field in
  type X` as a **version-drift** report, not a typo: the mod predates the game,
  the value is dropped, the def loads anyway, and the instance count is the

## 3. Pick the implementation tier before you pick the code

Most "how do I do X in RimWorld" questions are really "at which layer does X
belong". Getting this wrong is expensive — people write a C# mod for something a
six-line XML patch does, or try to patch a def for something that only exists at
runtime. Work down this ladder and stop at the first tier that can do the job:

| Tier | Layer | Use when the thing must… | Cost to change later |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | Mod list / settings / scenario | be true before worldgen | free |
| b | XML Def patch | be *true of the game* — stats, spawns, recipes, names | cheap |
| c | C# / Harmony assembly | *behave* differently — new mechanics, new AI | expensive |
| d | Save-game edit | be true of one existing colony, retroactively | one-shot, risky |
| e | Live runtime manipulation (bridge/console) | *change during play* | ephemeral |
| f | External host-side tooling | analyse or generate outside the game | free |

The rule of thumb that keeps this straight: **bake what must be TRUE, script
what must be PLACED, run live only what must CHANGE.** If a value never varies
during a playthrough, it belongs in tier b, full stop. Reaching for C# because
XML feels weak is the single most common overbuild in this domain.

⚠️ **Prove a comp exists before scoping tier b around it:** `grep -rln
"CompProperties_<Name>" "$RW/Data"`. Zero hits means the mechanic is stat-driven
or hard-coded in the `thingClass` — there is no `CompProperties_ShieldBelt` in
1.6; `Apparel_ShieldBelt` is plain `Apparel` and the shield is entirely
`EnergyShieldEnergyMax` + `EnergyShieldRechargeRate`. Zero hits moves the job to
tier c, which rides a game load alone instead of batching.

## 5. Validate before you deploy

Run the bundled validator on any patch file before it goes near the Mods folder.
It catches the silent failures, which otherwise cost a full game restart to find.

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_patch.py path/to/Patch.xml \
    --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Data" \
    --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/workshop/content/294100" \
    --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Mods"
```

🔴 **Pass the Mods folder too** — first-party mods live there, not in Workshop
content (`references/patch-operations.md` has the failure this avoids).

The valuable check is the last one: it **runs each xpath against the real Defs on
disk and reports how many nodes it hits**. Zero hits means the patch would silently
do nothing; more hits than expected means a `Remove` is about to take out more than
you think. (Its other five checks are in `references/patch-operations.md`.)

A patch that validates clean can still be wrong about *intent*, so also confirm
in-game: load, then check the dev console (or `Player.log`) for the patch's own
name. Silence is success.

### Two things it cannot see

It reads defs **unpatched**, so a node another mod creates at runtime is invisible
and **0 matches can be the correct answer**; and it checks field names in no file,
so a hand-authored Def with a field that moved between versions sails straight
through. Both are in `references/patch-operations.md`, with the WeatherDef that
shipped a renamed field.

## 7. Debugging from Player.log

`%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\Player.log`

Triage by **consequence, not by position in the file**. The ladder, worst first:
static-constructor / `TypeInitializationException` / `ReflectionTypeLoadException`
(the mod is *dead*, not noisy) → `Could not execute post-long-event action` (costs
exactly that one action; the queue continues) → `Could not resolve cross-reference`
(benign **or** fatal — it depends entirely on the `wanter`) →
`Patch operation … failed` (a no-op) → translation and sound errors (cosmetic).

⚠️ **The op named in a patch error is the WRAPPER, not the failure.**
`PatchOperationFindMod(Asimov) failed` was a broken *inner* `Replace`, not a
missing Asimov: `FindMod` returns the inner result while `ToString()` prints the
outer, and a genuinely absent mod returns **true** and logs nothing at all. Read
the inner op — and note that a field sitting at its C# default (`isOrganic`) has
no node for `Replace` to find, which is why `Conditional` is the safe default.

**`references/player-log-triage.md` has each rung in full: the greps, the IL-level
evidence for what each error actually costs, the two shapes of cross-reference
damage, and the judged-safe list you must keep.** Open it whenever you are reading
a log — five "benign" cross-reference lines were the sole cause of a dead mod for
three loads running, and a `ReflectionTypeLoadException` is usually load order
rather than a broken assembly.

## 8. C# mods, briefly

Reach for C# only when tier (c) is genuinely required — see §3. When you do,
`references/csharp-and-loading.md` covers Harmony patch types, the entry-point
classes and their required constructor signatures, and `LoadFolders.xml`. Two
constructor rules cause a disproportionate share of "mod does nothing" reports:

- A `GameComponent` needs a **public constructor taking `(Game game)`**. Without
  it, `Game.FillComponents` throws `MissingMethodException` and the component
  silently never exists — worse than a crash, because the feature appears to
  work and simply has no consequences.
- A `Mod` subclass needs `(ModContentPack content)`.

🔴 **Every mod we ship carries a real Mod Settings screen** (owner ruling,
2026-09-12, `MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1`): on/off per major feature or mechanic,
tuning where a number is the experience, defaults equal to shipped behaviour,
all-off degrading gracefully, and any worldgen-affecting toggle labelled as
such. Biome-kit mechanics get feature-gated so they can be enabled in a
different biome without the whole kit. This is standard `Mod` +
`ModSettings` — a settings class holding the fields, a `Mod` subclass
exposing `DoSettingsWindowContents` and calling `settings.Write()`, and every
gated feature reading its own field rather than a hardcoded constant.
Applies to every mod going forward, not just a retrofit pass.

⚠️ **`FilthMaker` refuses `Filth_AnimalFilth` on ALL natural terrain**
(`placementMask [Terrain]` vs `filthAcceptanceMask [Unnatural]`) — a comp's
filth drop is a silent no-op outdoors, and "the comp ticked with no filth
appearing" is not evidence the comp is broken.

⚠️ **A subprocess wrapper that only reads `stderr` on a nonzero exit can miss
the real error entirely if the process writes it to `stdout` instead.** A C#
wrapper around an external CLI produced an empty, useless diagnostic on a real
auth failure because that failure printed to stdout, not stderr. Capture and
surface BOTH streams on any subprocess failure; never assume the error
channel.

---
- **C# builds work from WSL; do not believe "this WSL machine cannot compile the .csproj".** There is no Visual Studio, NuGet CLI or .NET Framework targeting pack, and none is needed. The SDK is user-local at `C:\Users\Mandrake\.dotnet\dotnet.exe` (no admin, not on PATH; `C:\Program Files\dotnet` is runtime-only and will not build). From WSL: `/mnt/c/Users/Mandrake/.dotnet/dotnet.exe build 'D:\Luke\dev\Rimworld\src\...\Foo.csproj' -c Release` (forward-slash binary, Windows-style project path) builds clean with no setup. `net472` targeting comes from the `Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies` NuGet package. Reference the game's DLLs in `RimWorldWin64_Data\Managed` with `<Private>false</Private>` so nothing is copied into the mod folder. Copy `mods/dev/RimDefDump/Source/RimDefDump.csproj` as the working reference. Any subagent brief that touches C# must state the invocation explicitly: the false "can't compile from WSL" claim, shipping C# build-unverified, is the most common false claim subagents produce.
