patches and defs The authoring surface itself — xpath, `PatchOperation*`, inheritance, `ParentName`, def shape and the fields the engine reads. **Read this one before writing a patch.** These are the traps that cost a game load rather than a rerun, because a bad patch fails *silently* and you find out 25 minutes later. What goes in, and what does not: `references/traps.md`. --- ### An animal registered into a biome from both directions crashes the biome's animal table **Symptom:** `System.ArgumentException: An item with the same key has already been added. Key: Armadillo`, thrown from `BiomeDef.CommonalityOfAnimal`. Three unrelated mods broke at once and none was the cause: Choose Wild Animal Spawns died in its static constructor, Giddy-Up logged "error calling AllWildAnimals … Skipping", Biome Compatibility Project threw inside the post-long-event queue. **Cause:** an animal reaches a biome two ways — the biome's `` list, or the animal's `` list — and both `Add()` into one dictionary keyed on PawnKindDef. Beasts of the Rim redefined vanilla `Armadillo` with `wildBiomes` entries Core already listed; separately the Titans mod listed `TropicalSwamp` **twice inside its own** `wildBiomes`. **Fix:** remove the **animal side** (``), never the biome side — the biome's list keeps the animal spawning at the biome's commonality, so nothing is lost. For a self-duplicate, `.../TropicalSwamp[2]` with the same predicate in the conditional test. An offline duplicate-scan of both directions across 1,168 animals takes seconds and found exactly three bad pairs. **Recurs when:** any engine field that is a `Dictionary` populated from two directions — the exception names the *key*, never the mod, so the log gives no attribution. --- --- - **A defect a PatchOperation CREATES is invisible to any reader of mod XML; ask the def dump capture, and treat its list as a floor.** Two mods' patches can each look fine on disk (one adds a biome to `race/wildBiomes`, ours adds the animal to the biome's `wildAnimals`) while the post-patch game collides. `DefDump/captures//defs/*.json` carries the post-patch fields; `src/RimMandrake/Utils/biome_animal_conflicts.py` is the worked example. The log undercounts structurally: `BiomeDef.CommonalityOfAnimal` throws at the first duplicate key per biome (the log named 12, the capture 27). The capture reports the engine's answer, not the field: `DefDumper.cs` serialises `CommonalityOfAnimal` inside a bare `catch { }`, the throw leaves a partial cache, and every animal never reached reads a plausible 0f (181 of 744 weights), so a computed zero can mean the computation died. The capture is also self-erasing: it is taken after every patch, so a defect a shipped patch already cured is invisible (56 found vs 61 shipped). Never ship a capture-derived list as the fix file; the shipped set stays the union of every pair ever found. - **Check three defects at every biome review before scoring it.** Seen in 5 of 7 grandfathered biomes: ratified creatures never built (art already done in artpipe); invented-name content stranded in the campaign tier (it belongs in the free tier); campaign patches that wholesale-Replace an `RM_` list or gate on a donor/`RUT_` twin def. ### `Inherit="False"` makes a correct patch a silent no-op **Symptom:** a rebalance patch aimed at an abstract base applied cleanly — zero errors in `Player.log` — yet only 7 of 15 lightsabers went to power 99 / AP 0, and 8 stayed at 26 / AP −1. Vanilla writes `Inherit="False"` **314 times**, 9 of them on `pawnGroupMakers` alone. If you did not write it, you appended. Three corollaries: - **Changing a parent to gain fields also inherits its lists.** Re-parenting to pick up art or namers silently drags the parent's group makers, comps and filters along with them. - Patching the abstract parent hits every descendant at once, including ones from mods you didn't consider. Powerful and easy to overreach with. - Sometimes the append is what you want — inheriting a vanilla faction's twelve group makers and adding a thirteenth is a legitimate, cheap design. Decide which you want; do not discover it. --- ## 6. Operation-by-operation notes ### Quick reference — what each operation takes | Class | Does | Needs | |---|---|---| | `PatchOperationAdd` | insert as **child** of target | `xpath`, `value`, opt. `order` | | `PatchOperationInsert` | insert as **sibling** of target | `xpath`, `value`, opt. `order` | | `PatchOperationReplace` | swap the node out | `xpath`, `value` | | `PatchOperationRemove` | delete **all** matches | `xpath` | | `PatchOperationAttributeAdd` / `Set` / `Remove` | attributes; `Add` won't overwrite | `xpath`, `attribute`, (`value`) | | `PatchOperationSetName` | rename node, keep contents | `xpath`, `name` | | `PatchOperationAddModExtension` | attach a DefModExtension | `xpath`, `value` | | `PatchOperationSequence` | run ops in order, **stop at first failure** | `operations` | | `PatchOperationConditional` | node exists? → `match` / `nomatch` | `xpath` | | `PatchOperationFindMod` | mod installed? → `match` / `nomatch` | `mods` | `PatchOperationTest` is obsolete; use `Conditional`. **`PatchOperationAdd`** — appends as a *child* of the target. `Prepend` puts it first instead. If the parent node doesn't exist yet, this fails; add the parent in a preceding op, or use a `Sequence`. **`PatchOperationInsert`** — inserts as a *sibling*, default before the target. Use when position among siblings matters (e.g. ordering `
  • ` entries in a `comps` list where a comp reads state left by an earlier one). **`PatchOperationReplace`** — the `` replaces the whole selected node, element name included, so the value must contain the element: ```xml 5.2 ``` A common mistake is supplying only the inner text, which silently produces a malformed def. **`PatchOperationRemove`** — deletes every match. See §4. **`PatchOperationAttributeAdd` / `Set` / `Remove`** — `Add` will not overwrite an existing attribute; `Set` will. Removing a stale `MayRequire` is a legitimate and underused way to fix an upstream guard that points at the wrong mod. **`PatchOperationSetName`** — renames the element, keeps the contents. The tool for dictionary-keyed fields: moving an animal from one biome to another is a `SetName` on `wildBiomes/Desert` → `AridShrubland`, not a remove-plus-add. **`PatchOperationAddModExtension`** — attaches a `DefModExtension`; creates the `modExtensions` node if absent. `` needs `Class="YourNamespace.YourExt"`. **`PatchOperationSequence`** — runs `` in order and **stops at the first failure**. Good: an atomic multi-step edit where later steps assume earlier ones. Bad: a grab-bag of unrelated ops, where one early failure silently cancels everything after it. Keep sequences short and related. **`PatchOperationConditional`** — `` is the test; `` and/or `` hold operations. This is the default wrapper for anything touching another mod's content. ---

## 4. The nursery, and a tier problem worth his ruling

The sheet's §4 first ring: the Grey Sea's roster **breeds here** — *"the young here, the
adults in the terminator waters"* — juveniles swarming the shallows, cheap to hunt, and the
arithmetic every scavenger knows: *"don't kill what's small here; its mother is why nobody goes
out onto the open water."* 🔴 **Corrected 2026-09-23 on the owner's word — there are no nautical
ships in this world**, so the sheet's original *"the reason ships sink"* was a dead metaphor and
is amended in `the_miasma.md` §4. ⚠️ `design/Jawa/campaign/CAMPAIGN_ARC_GATHER.md` G34 still
quotes the old phrasing and is now stale.

**Eight juvenile defs already ship** — `RSW_MeeJuv`, `RSW_FaaJuv`, `RSW_LaaJuv`,
`RSW_YobshrimpJuv`, `RSW_SiltLampreyJuv`, `RSW_RustNipperJuv`, `RSW_OpeeSeaKillerJuv`,
`RSW_DiggerJuvenile` — and seven of them are already cast on this biome. The nursery is the
one ring that is genuinely built.

### 🔴 But every one of them is campaign-tier, and that breaks a standing rule

`sea_beasts_roster.md` is tagged **Tier RimStarWars (`RSW_`)** in its entirety. ⇒ The
franchise-free `mandrake.rm.miasma` would ship with **no nursery at all** — no juveniles, no
crowded shallows, and therefore (per §5) no stranded either. That directly contradicts the
owner's ruling of 2026-09-22:

> *"The top mod without star wars will look precisely the same as the star wars enhanced one
> save for any star wars beasts we populate it with."*

…and the corollary already written into the project's own instructions: **a `RM_` biome does
not get a thin dependency-free fallback roster.**

### ⭐ And the fix is nearly free, because most of that roster is not Star Wars at all

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a headless Whittle session and apply its existing Stop-hook checker.

Exit 0 only when that checker permits a stop. A blocked/incomplete claim is
exit 1; an explicit BLOCKED/STOP is exit 2. Codex failures never invoke Claude.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tools"))
import role_runner


def validate(cwd, invoke=subprocess.run):
    cwd = Path(cwd).resolve()
    work = cwd / os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR", "whittle")
    if not (work / "STATEMENT.md").is_file():
        raise ValueError("Whittle requires whittle/STATEMENT.md")
    if (work / "STOP").exists() or ((work / "BLOCKED.md").is_file() and (work / "BLOCKED.md").read_text().strip()):
        return 2
    hook = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "template/whittle_stop.py"
    env = dict(os.environ, WHITTLE="1", CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=str(cwd))
    proc = invoke([sys.executable, str(hook)], input=json.dumps({"cwd": str(cwd), "stop_hook_active": False,
                  "session_id": "headless-validator"}), text=True, capture_output=True, env=env, cwd=cwd, timeout=60)
    if proc.returncode:
        return 1
    if proc.stdout.strip():
        decision = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        if decision.get("decision") == "block":
            print(decision.get("reason", "incomplete"), file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        raise ValueError("unexpected Whittle checker output")
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--runner", choices=("claude", "codex"), default="claude")
    ap.add_argument("--cwd", default=".")
    ap.add_argument("--log", default="whittle/run.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--model")
    ap.add_argument("--effort")
    ap.add_argument("--sandbox")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cwd = Path(a.cwd).resolve()
    prompt = (cwd / os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR", "whittle") / "PROMPT.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    rc = role_runner.run(a.runner, cwd, prompt, cwd / a.log, model=a.model, effort=a.effort,
                         sandbox=a.sandbox, claude_args=("--output-format", "json", "--dangerously-skip-permissions"))
    return rc if rc else validate(cwd)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline lint of one RimMandrake mod: XML defs/patches against its C# source. No game, no build. Generalised from
lint_scarlands_defs.py (the helpers are imported from it); the per-mod wrappers are lint_<mod>_defs.py.

    python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/lint_mod_defs.py <ModFolder> [--mod-dir <dir>] [--quiet]

Exit 1 on any ERROR, 2 if UNMEASURED. WARN lines are dead/unwired things worth a look but not necessarily wrong.
Checks: class-resolves, fields-match, driver-kind, getnamed-resolves, defof-resolves, settings-scribed (key == field,
Scribe default == initializer, Scribed once, dead toggles, no control), compile-listed (EnableDefaultCompileItems is
false: a missing Compile line compiles into nothing, silently), wired, defname-unique, texpath-resolves.
"""
import os
import re
import sys
import glob
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from lint_scarlands_defs import (SRC, OUR_PREFIX, CLASS_ELEMS, STRICT_ROOTS, strip_comments, Cls,  # noqa: E402
                                 scan_csharp, chain, issubclass_name)


class SiblingText(str):
    """Text of every other mod's defs/patches; `name in text` is a whole-identifier test."""
    def __contains__(self, name):
        return re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(name) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])", str(self)) is not None


def run(mod_name, argv, known_missing_art=(), require_xml=True, require_settings=True, instance_settings=False):
    mod = os.path.join(SRC, mod_name)
    if "--mod-dir" in argv:
        mod = argv[argv.index("--mod-dir") + 1]
    quiet = "--quiet" in argv
    errs, warns = [], []
    E = lambda chk, msg: errs.append(f"ERROR {chk}: {msg}")
    W = lambda chk, msg: warns.append(f"WARN  {chk}: {msg}")

    our = scan_csharp(os.path.join(mod, "Source"))
    allc = scan_csharp(SRC)
    defs_xml = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(mod, "Defs", "**", "*.xml"), recursive=True))
    patch_xml = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(mod, "Patches", "**", "*.xml"), recursive=True))
    sanity = {"xml": len(defs_xml) + len(patch_xml), "classes": len([k for k in our if "." not in k])}
    if (sanity["xml"] == 0 and require_xml) or sanity["classes"] == 0:
        print(f"LINT UNMEASURED: found {sanity} - wrong --mod-dir?")
        return 2

"""
import collections
import os
import pathlib
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import biome_group_sizes as bgs  # noqa: E402

SRC = bgs.ROOT / "src"
SKIP = ("selftest_fixtures", "Backup", "backup", "_archive", "retired")


def repeats(root):
    """(defName, tag, count) for every top-level def under a <Defs> root that repeats a direct child."""
    out = []
    if root.tag != "Defs":
        return out
    for d in root:
        if not isinstance(d.tag, str):
            continue
        tags = collections.Counter(ch.tag for ch in d if isinstance(ch.tag, str))
        for tag, n in tags.items():
            if n > 1:
                out.append((d.findtext("defName") or d.get("Name") or d.tag, tag, n))
    return out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Whittle's Stop hook: the session is asked to keep working until its files show the work is done, with evidence.

Claude Code runs this when the agent tries to end a turn. It reads the hook JSON on stdin and either prints nothing
(the turn ends) or prints {"decision": "block", "reason": ...}, which hands the reason back to the agent as its next
instruction.

Armed only in a session started with WHITTLE=1 in its environment, in a project with <project>/whittle/STATEMENT.md.
Other sessions in the same project are untouched. While armed, a turn may end only when one of these holds:

  whittle/STOP exists            the owner's off switch. Stays until deleted.
  whittle/BLOCKED.md has text    the agent's way out ("I'm blocked, here's why", or a question for the owner). Filed in
                                 whittle/history/ and the hook re-arms, so one blocked stop doesn't disarm the session.
  the claim is complete          DONE.md has one "true" line per statement bullet; every evidence file it names is a
                                 regular file inside the project and newer than the last change to the project's files;
                                 BROADEN.md has text; JUDGE.md is newer than DONE.md and every evidence file and ends
                                 with the line "would show: yes"; NOTES.md is not newer than DONE.md.
  refusals ran out               LOOP_LIMIT refusals in a row with the same problems and no change to the project. The
                                 turn ends and whittle/STALLED.md says so. A stop the agent makes on its own (not one
                                 driven by this hook, per Claude Code's stop_hook_active) starts the count again.

What it checks is files, not behaviour: who wrote JUDGE.md or BROADEN.md, and whether the evidence shows anything, it
cannot tell. Freshness is by modification time (directories included, so deletions count); an edit that preserves
mtimes is invisible to it. Any unexpected error blocks with the error as the reason, under the same refusal limit.

Stdlib only. Optional settings: WHITTLE_DIR, WHITTLE_LOOP_LIMIT, WHITTLE_NEED_JUDGE=0, WHITTLE_NEED_BROADEN=0.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ARM = "WHITTLE"
VERDICT = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s*(true|false|unseen|cannot tell)\s*:\s*(.+)$", re.I)
EVIDENCE = re.compile(r"\|\s*evidence\s*:(.*)$", re.I)
BACKTICK = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")
HIDDEN = re.compile(r"<!--.*?-->|^(```|~~~).*?^\1[^\n]*$", re.S | re.M)


def settings():
    work = os.path.normpath(os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR", "whittle")).replace("\\", "/").strip("/")
    if not work or work.startswith("..") or os.path.isabs(work):
        raise ValueError("WHITTLE_DIR must be a folder inside the project, got %r" % os.environ.get("WHITTLE_DIR"))
    limit = int(os.environ.get("WHITTLE_LOOP_LIMIT", "3"))
    return work, max(limit, 1), os.environ.get("WHITTLE_NEED_JUDGE", "1") != "0", \
        os.environ.get("WHITTLE_NEED_BROADEN", "1") != "0"


def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip().lower()


def read(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()


def has_text(path):
    return os.path.isfile(path) and read(path).strip() != ""


def statement_lines(path):
    """The frozen statement's bullet lines ('- ...' or '* ...'), outside comments and code fences."""
    return [norm(m.group(1)) for m in re.finditer(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(.+)$", HIDDEN.sub("", read(path)), re.M)]


def mtime(path):
    try:
        return os.stat(path).st_mtime
    except OSError:
        return None


def project_files(root):
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard", "-z"],
                             capture_output=True, timeout=30, check=True).stdout
        return [os.fsdecode(f) for f in out.split(b"\0") if f]
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        files = []
        for d, dirs, names in os.walk(root):
            dirs[:] = [x for x in dirs if x != ".git"]
            files += [os.path.relpath(os.path.join(d, n), root).replace(os.sep, "/") for n in names]
        return files


def last_change(root, work):
    """Newest mtime among the project's files and their folders, outside the Whittle folder. A folder's mtime moves
    when a file in it is added, deleted or renamed, so a deletion counts as a change."""
    skip = work + "/"
    paths = set()
    for f in project_files(root):
        if (f + "/").startswith(skip):
            continue
        paths.add(f)
        d = os.path.dirname(f)
        while d:
            paths.add(d)
            d = os.path.dirname(d)
    times = [mtime(os.path.join(root, p)) for p in paths] + [mtime(root)]
    return max([t for t in times if t is not None], default=0.0)


def evidence_problem(root, rel):
    """None if `rel` names a regular file inside the project, else what is wrong with it."""
    if os.path.isabs(rel) or re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]:", rel):
        return "'%s' is an absolute path; name evidence relative to the project" % rel
    real_root = os.path.realpath(root)
    real = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, rel))
    if os.path.commonpath([real_root, real]) != real_root:
        return "'%s' points outside the project" % rel
    if not os.path.isfile(real):
        return "'%s' is not a file that exists" % rel
    return None


def done_problems(root, work, need_judge, need_broaden):
    """Everything standing between this session and a finished turn. Empty means the claim is complete."""
    w = lambda name: os.path.join(root, work, name)
    wanted = statement_lines(w("STATEMENT.md"))
    if not wanted:
        return ["%s/STATEMENT.md has no bullet lines ('- ...'), so there is nothing to check a claim against. Ask the "
                "owner to fix it: write %s/BLOCKED.md and stop." % (work, work)]
    if not os.path.isfile(w("DONE.md")):
        return ["There is no %s/DONE.md yet. Keep working. When you would show this to the owner, write it: one line per "
                "statement bullet, '- true: <the bullet, copied> | evidence: `path` `path`', naming saved evidence files."
                % work]
    rows, problems = {}, []
    for line in HIDDEN.sub("", read(w("DONE.md"))).splitlines():
        m = VERDICT.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text, ev = m.group(2), ""
        e = EVIDENCE.search(text)
        if e:
            text, ev = text[:e.start()], e.group(1)
        key = norm(text)
        if key in rows:
            problems.append("DONE.md has two verdict lines for '%s'. Keep one." % key)
        rows[key] = (m.group(1).lower(), BACKTICK.findall(ev))
    changed = last_change(root, work)
    evidence_times = []
    for line in wanted:
        if line not in rows:
            problems.append("DONE.md has no verdict line for the statement bullet '%s'. Copy the bullet exactly." % line)
            continue
        verdict, paths = rows[line]
        if verdict != "true":
            problems.append("'%s' is marked %s. Make it true, or write %s/BLOCKED.md saying why you can't." % (line, verdict, work))
            continue
        if not paths:
            problems.append("'%s' names no evidence (put paths in backticks after '| evidence:')." % line)
            continue
        for p in paths:
            bad = evidence_problem(root, p)
            if bad:
                problems.append("Evidence for '%s': %s." % (line, bad))
                continue
            t = mtime(os.path.join(root, p))
            evidence_times.append(t)
            if t < changed:
                problems.append("The evidence '%s' for '%s' is older than your last change to the project. Look again "
                                "and save fresh evidence." % (p, line))
    done_t = mtime(w("DONE.md"))
    notes_t = mtime(w("NOTES.md"))
    if notes_t and notes_t > done_t:
        problems.append("The owner's notes (%s/NOTES.md) changed after DONE.md was written. Reread them, act on them, and "
                        "write DONE.md again." % work)
    if need_broaden and not has_text(w("BROADEN.md")):
        problems.append("No %s/BROADEN.md. Ask a different model what a real user would try that you haven't, try the "
                        "most revealing one or two, and write the question, the answer and what you found there." % work)
    if need_judge:
        judge_t = mtime(w("JUDGE.md"))
        if not os.path.isfile(w("JUDGE.md")) or judge_t < max([done_t] + evidence_times):
            problems.append("No judge's verdict newer than DONE.md and the evidence. Spawn a fresh subagent (not a fork) "
                            "with %s/JUDGE_PROMPT.md as its whole brief. It writes %s/JUDGE.md." % (work, work))
        else:
            lines = [l.strip().lower() for l in read(w("JUDGE.md")).splitlines() if l.strip()]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline: validation.sea_catch_alive_checks() is green on the shipped defs and goes red when a sea loses a
floor body, a catch breaks the RM_<X>Catch pairing, or a body is wired but never defined.

    python3 src/RimMandrake/TerminalBiomes/selftest_sea_catch_alive.py
"""
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "..", "Utils"))
import validation as V  # noqa: E402

FAILS = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    print("%s  %s %s" % ("ok  " if cond else "FAIL", name, "" if cond else detail))
    if not cond:
        FAILS.append(name)


def mutated(rel, old, new):
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seacatch_")
    dst = os.path.join(tmp, "Defs")
    shutil.copytree(os.path.join(HERE, "Defs"), dst)
    p = os.path.join(dst, rel)
    s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
    assert old in s, (rel, old)
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(old, new, 1))
    return tmp, dst


shipped = V.sea_catch_alive_checks()
check("shipped: every catch in the four seas has a living floor body", not shipped, str(shipped[:5]))
for label, rel, old, new in [
    ("twilight niim body unwired", "BiomeDefs/RM_TwilightSea.xml", "<RM_Niim>1.0</RM_Niim>", ""),
    ("grey body unwired", "BiomeDefs/RM_GreySea.xml", "<RM_Nissik>0.9</RM_Nissik>", ""),
    ("catch breaks pairing", "BiomeDefs/RM_TwilightSea.xml", "<RM_KelluCatch>1</RM_KelluCatch>", "<RM_Kellu_Item>1</RM_Kellu_Item>"),
    ("body wired but undefined", "ThingDefs_Races/RM_TwilightSeaFloorLife.xml", "<defName>RM_Liiru</defName>\n    <label>", "<defName>RM_LiiruGone</defName>\n    <label>"),
]:
    tmp, dst = mutated(rel, old, new)
    try:
        bad = V.sea_catch_alive_checks(dst)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp)
    check("mutant %-26s goes red" % label, bool(bad), "")
print("\n%s" % ("ALL OK" if not FAILS else "FAILED: %s" % FAILS))
sys.exit(1 if FAILS else 0)

## Inheritance, changes and consumers

The complete selected ThingDef chains are `BasePawn → AnimalThingBase → RM_Reefback → RM_ReefbackJuv` and `BasePawn → AnimalThingBase → RM_WardenMother`. The kind chains are `AnimalKindBase → RM_Reefback_Kind → RM_ReefbackJuv` and `AnimalKindBase → RM_WardenMother`. Installed Core `Defs/ThingDefs_Races/Races_Animal_Base.xml` supplies all three base nodes. The adult source is sea-beast XML lines 1314–1430; the young is lines 1840–1918; [mother XML](../../src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_WardenMother.xml) supplies the mother and elder stage. The same inputs are retained under [raw/final/inputs](evidence/raw/final/inputs.json).

Direct comparison of the before/current sea files found **34 top-level definitions in each, with exactly two changed nodes**, the young ThingDef and kind. Within those nodes the changes are exactly: expanded thin-crust description; added sharp/blunt/heat armor 0.30/0.25/0.30; replacement tools 16/10 with cooldowns 3/2.5 and bulk chanceFactor0.3; baseHealthScale8; combatPower150. Tools use `Inherit="False"`; statBases merge. Adult tools480/120, health20, size32, armor0.70/0.60/0.75 and kindPower2000 remain. The mother's file and both biome files are byte-identical to their raw before snapshots. The young's age table, graphic stages and group2~3 also compare unchanged.

Inherited source values retained by the calf include MoveSpeed2, MarketValue8000, comfy temperatures−30/50, Wildness1, Pinniped body, sealskin leather, waterSeeker, waterCellCost1, foodTypeNone, disableMating, canBePredatorPreyfalse, manhunterOnDamageChance0.2, lifeExpectancy500, ecosystemWeight4 and kind water-speed factor2. The current Miasma row is0.15; Grey Sea adult row0.005. Neither density6.5 nor ecosystemWeight4 nor group2~3 is a population count. Parent and child graphic stages are separate from combat stage factors.

Installed Core `Defs/Misc/LifeStageDefs/LifeStages.xml` lines176–222 gives baby body/health/melee factors **0.2/0.25/0.5**, juvenile **0.5/0.6/0.75**, and adult constructor defaults1. The elder specifies body factor1 and inherits health/melee constructor defaults1. These defaults are verified in `RimWorld.LifeStageDef::.ctor` in the retained IL, not guessed from missing XML.

The production consumer chain is `Tool.AdjustedBaseMeleeDamageAmount → VerbProperties.AdjustedMeleeDamageAmount → GetDamageFactorFor → Verb_MeleeAttackDamage.DamageInfosToApply` (including its iterator `MoveNext`). For healthy natural linked parts with no equipment/hediff/gene modifiers it uses tool power × linked-part efficiency1 × stage melee factor × `MeleeDamageFactor`1. Installed Core `Defs/Stats/Stats_Pawns_Combat.xml` lines20–34 gives that stat's default1 and an Anomaly shambler-crawling modifier, excluded by the healthy/unmodified premise. The actual damage iterator subsequently applies a **0.8–1.2 random multiplier**, followed by damage/armor processing. Therefore the table reports nominal adjusted damage, not exact realized hits. Damage-derived armor penetration, damaged linked parts, tool selection, misses and downstream injury mechanics also matter. See [engine-final.stdout.txt](evidence/raw/engine-final.stdout.txt), methods beginning at lines91,912,1012,1109,1209.

`Pawn.BodySize` is baseBodySize × stage bodySizeFactor; `Pawn.HealthScale` instead uses baseHealthScale × healthScaleFactor. `BodyPartDef.GetMaxHealth` multiplies the part's base hitPoints by HealthScale and takes `CeilToInt`. Installed Odyssey `Defs/Bodies/Bodies_Animal_Pinniped.xml` has corePart Body and both linked groups, HeadAttackTool and FrontLeftPaw. Installed Core body parts supply Body40, Brain10 and Heart15. Body is one part, not the pawn's total health pool. See retained IL lines719–727,892–911 and the installed snapshots in `raw/final/inputs/installed/Data/`.

I also checked a real override omitted by the instrument's narrow health-getter search: [RM_ForgeDhoggurSwell.cs](../../src/RimMandrake/TheForge/Source/RM_ForgeDhoggurSwell.cs), lines243–315, patches `Pawn.HealthScale` and `BodySize`. It multiplies only pawns in the swell registry; registration is through the swell comp. None of these selected resolved races has that comp or the swell hediff. It does not alter the healthy selected model. The named Pyrelands health rewrite applies to FurnaceBeast, and Greentide combatPower writes apply to its ant kinds. This is an explicit dismissal after reading their guards, not a claim that runtime patches cannot exist.

`combatPower` does not multiply attack damage or health. The installed `PawnGenOption.get_Cost` reads it for generation cost (IL lines72–76). Local [RM_PitBuyer.cs](../../src/RimMandrake/KeelHoist/Source/RM_PitBuyer.cs), lines46–52, reads it for beast fighter classification; its kernel threshold is100, so both150 and2000 qualify. Pyrelands arrival selection filters canArriveManhunter, which the calf still inherits asfalse. Thus150 is profile/cost metadata, not evidence for lower hits or a demonstrated population effect.

Two hypothetical ranged hunters each fire damage12, sharp AP0.15, every3 seconds, hit probability0.60, at a healthy naked target. These are illustrative inputs fixed in `design_prompt.txt` before the remedy, not a named weapon or measured pawn. ## Design reconciliation and limits

The governing [the_miasma.md](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_miasma.md), lines97–127, promises cheap young, catastrophic parents and a dangerous water-bound resident guard. [the_grey_deep.md](../../design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_grey_deep.md), lines101–107, locates the adult's heavy crust in its centuries at sea. The independent remedy's thin-crusted nursery prey, catastrophic adult and intermediate adult/elder mother health profile fit those constraints without shrinking the calf or replacing residents. The current fauna specification§4 correctly keeps size and health separate and narrows cheap to the explicit model. The owner’s no-growth-campaign wording in that specification's successor section remains compatible with a permanently juvenile calf. Old JSON roster notes about mother placement,50% hurt revenge and historical names are not measurements of the current XML.

I **reject** two incidental claims in `design_raw.json/result`§§1,4–5: “wounds rather than kills” is not guaranteed, and its5.6/4.4 damaging-hit counts in30 seconds count one hunter. With20 total shots the stipulated unretaliated model gives11.1/8.7 expected damaging hits. Those counts still cannot establish production manhunter probabilities. Its71%/62% figures are not accepted as either correct team-model calculations or observations. The current nursery combat paragraph makes neither claim, so these errors do not require a different stat remedy or fail the frozen L0 work. Likewise its contact totals are illustrative nominal quotients, not hard bounds. This judgment accepts the narrowed specification explicitly, not the raw response wholesale.

Mother radius16 is a configured anchor-duty radius, not a measured attack radius or global calf-death trigger. [RM_CompTerritorialAnchor.cs](../../src/RimMandrake/EnvironmentalHazards/Source/RM_CompTerritorialAnchor.cs), lines265–340, uses existing defense/tolerance and water-or-adjacent-water target rules. [RM_CompWaterLocked.cs](../../src/RimMandrake/EnvironmentalHazards/Source/RM_CompWaterLocked.cs) has a periodic recovery/backstop, not a proof that no path ever crosses land. Existing stranded-young calls can issue a mother Goto (`Miasma/Source/RM_MapComponent_YoungCall.cs`); I therefore do not infer an absolute radius16 movement cage. Existing young damage breaks its crèche record (`RM_WardenMotherSuccession.cs:163–177`), while mother death despoils her marker (`EnvironmentalHazards/Source/RM_CompCrecheMarker.cs:60–88`). None of this newly implements remote revenge for killing an ordinary calf.

**Mechanism/defect disposition:** the checked remedy adds no gameplay mechanism. It uses ordinary inherited animal melee, health, natural armor and kind metadata. The old combat/spec inversion is proven in source and corrected locally; it was never proven an actual hunting failure. The discovered swell override is inapplicable under the checked premise. Existing mother land-crossing limitations and fiction/size/age tensions remain limitations, not newly repaired or newly accepted functionality. No new retaliation, water-pathing or maturation mechanism is being accepted without proof. No new live gate is warranted by these two explicit L0 criteria.
